title: proto_tcp Module
content_markdown:
The **proto\_tcp** module is a built-in transport module which implements SIP TCP-based communication. It does not handle TCP connections management, but only offers higher-level primitives to read and write SIP messages over TCP.

Once loaded, you will be able to define TCP listeners in your script, by adding its IP, and optionally the listening port, in your configuration file, similar to this example:

...
socket=tcp:127.0.0.1 		# change the listening IP
socket=tcp:127.0.0.1:5080	# change with the listening IP and port
...

exported_parameters.name: tcp_port
exported_parameters.description:
The default port to be used for all TCP related operation. Be careful as the default port impacts both the SIP listening part (if no port is defined in the TCP listeners) and the SIP sending part (if the destination URI has no explicit port).

If you want to change only the listening port for TCP, use the port option in the SIP listener defintion.

exported_parameters.name: tcp_send_timeout
exported_parameters.description: Time in milliseconds after a TCP connection will be closed if it is not available for blocking writing in this interval (and OpenSIPS wants to send something on it).

exported_parameters.name: tcp_max_msg_chunks
exported_parameters.description: The maximum number of chunks that a SIP message is expected to arrive via TCP. If a packet is received more fragmented than this, the connection is dropped (either the connection is very overloaded and this leads to high fragmentation - or we are the victim of an ongoing attack where the attacker is sending the traffic very fragmented in order to decrease our performance).

exported_parameters.name: tcp_crlf_pingpong
exported_parameters.description: Send CRLF pong (\r\n) to incoming CRLFCRLF ping messages over TCP. By default it is enabled (1).

exported_parameters.name: tcp_crlf_drop
exported_parameters.description: Drop CRLF (\r\n) ping messages. When this parameter is enabled, the TCP layer drops packets that contains a single CRLF message. If a CRLFCRLF message is received, it is handled according to the _tcp\_crlf\_pingpong_ parameter.

exported_parameters.name: tcp_async
exported_parameters.description: If the TCP connect and write operations should be done in an asynchronous mode (non-blocking connect and write). If disabled, OpenSIPS will block and wait for TCP operations like connect and write.

exported_parameters.name: tcp_async_max_postponed_chunks
exported_parameters.description: If tcp_async is enabled, this specifies the maximum number of SIP messages that can be stashed for later/async writing. If the connection pending writes exceed this number, the connection will be marked as broken and dropped.

exported_parameters.name: tcp_async_local_write_timeout
exported_parameters.description: If tcp_async is enabled, this specifies the number of milliseconds that a write op will be tried in blocking mode (optimization). If the write operation lasts more than this, the write will go to async mode and will be passed to TCP MAIN for polling.

exported_parameters.name: trace_destination
exported_parameters.description: Trace destination as defined in the tracing module. Currently the only tracing module is proto_hep. Network events such as connect, accept and connection closed events shall be traced along with errors that could appear in the process.
exported_parameters.notes: WARNING: A tracing module must be loaded in order for this parameter to work. (for example proto_hep).

exported_parameters.name: trace_on
exported_parameters.description: This controls whether tracing for tcp is on or not. You still need to define Section 1.3.9, “trace_destination (string)” in order to work, but this value will be controlled using mi function Section 1.4.1, “ tcp_trace ”.

exported_parameters.name: trace_filter_route
exported_parameters.description: Define the name of a route in which you can filter which connections will be trace and which connections won't be. In this route you will have information regarding source and destination ips and ports for the current connection. To disable tracing for a specific connection the last call in this route must be **drop**, any other exit mode resulting in tracing the current connection ( of course you still have to define a [Section�1.3.9, “`trace_destination` (string)”](#trace-destination "1.3.9.�trace_destination (string)") and trace must be on at the time this connection is opened.
exported_parameters.notes:
**IMPORTANT** Filtering on ip addresses and ports can be made using **$si** and **$sp** for matching either the entity that is connecting to OpenSIPS or the entity to which OpenSIPS is connecting. The name might be misleading ( **$si** meaning the source ip if you read the docs) but in reality it is simply the socket other than the OpenSIPS socket. In order to match OpenSIPS interface (either the one that accepted the connection or the one that initiated a connection) **$socket\_in(ip)** (ip) and **$socket\_in(port)** (port) can be used.

**WARNING:** IF [Section�1.3.10, “`trace_on` (int)”](#trace-on "1.3.10.�trace_on (int)") is set to 0 or tracing is deactived via the mi command [Section�1.4.1, “ `tcp_trace` ”](#tcp-trace "1.4.1.� tcp_trace") this route won't be called.
